Q7. Early in 1749 the chaplain at Fort St David, Francis Fordyce, publicly insulted Robert Clive, leading to his dismissal, and replacement by Y. He was starting to amass a small fortune, but the directors of the Company soon instructed him to confine himself to his religious duties. This did not sit well and he returned to England. When George Pigot resigned in November 1763, it made way for Y to take up the post of Governor of Madras. With his new-found authority he entered more deeply into the world of trade, enlarging his personal wealth all the time. he eventually left India in January 1767 at the age of 50 and was well received by both King George III and the Court of Directors on his return. We, however, know X for a geographic reason than historic. ID X
